# Beyond the static plot {#sec-beyond-static}

Sometimes a plot wants to move, or wants the reader to poke at it.

Neither is core to making better graphs, and both eat time, so they live here
rather than in the day. If we've got time at the end I'll demo them. If not,
they're here when you want them.

::: {.overview}

## Animation with gganimate

<!-- Animation is a channel like any other, and it is the most expensive one.
     It works when the thing changing is time and the reader needs to feel the
     change. It fails as a substitute for small multiples, which is what most
     animated plots should have been.

     Cross reference @sec-comparing.

     The honest demo is the pedestrian year animated by month against the same
     thing faceted by month. The facets win, and I should say so while showing
     my own animation losing. gapminder over time is the case where animation
     genuinely helps, and it is the one everybody has seen.

     gganimate is NOT in the main setup install list, it is in the optional
     block in schedule.md. Say that at the top of the section so nobody stalls
     on an install mid-demo. It also needs a renderer (gifski or av), which is
     the usual failure and worth naming. -->

## Interactive graphics with ggiraph

<!-- Tooltips and hover, which are genuinely useful when a plot has more detail
     than fits on the page. The trap is using interactivity to avoid making a
     decision about what matters, which is the same failure @sec-colour is about.

     The one-line version: geom_point_interactive(aes(tooltip = sensor_name))
     plus girafe(). Close to free if they already have the ggplot.

     Two things worth saying, because both cost people real time:
       - a tooltip does not exist in a PDF or a printed paper, so anything you
         only put in a tooltip is invisible to half your readers
       - plotly::ggplotly() is the other route, and it silently drops parts of
         a ggplot it cannot translate. ggiraph is more faithful.

     This appendix only renders usefully in HTML. Guard the chunks the same way
     the countdown timers are guarded in @sec-computed:
       #| eval: !expr knitr::is_html_output()
     if the PDF format ever comes back on in _quarto.yml. -->
